title: VLT's Laser Guide Star
caption: A laser guide star beam and the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: An orange beam of light rises from one of the 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes of ESO's Very Large Telescope, and beyond it the Milky Way shows off its fine structure, with dark lanes of dust woven among patches of faint, glowing gas. The VLT stands at the Paranal Observatory in northern Chile.

ESO calls the orange glow unmistakable. It comes from a Laser Guide Star, a beam that creates an artificial point of light high in the sky. Telescopes use such a point as a reference for adaptive optics, a technique for correcting the blurring caused by Earth's turbulent atmosphere.

Behind the beam, the band of our galaxy is on full display. The dark lanes are clouds of dust that block the light of stars behind them, while the fainter glowing areas are gas giving off light of its own.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way's dust lanes and faint glowing gas appear far more clearly here than in person.
